item.title: Artifacts

Cortex publishes JVM modules and container deployment assets separately.

Maven Artifacts

See Maven Artifacts for the BOM-backed module list and node dependencies.

item.title: Configuration
item.description: Cortex is a daemon and is configured primarily through environment variables, which is convenient for container-based deployments. A cortex CLI wrapper (picocli) also exists for local runs, but in a typical online deployment you just set environment variables and start the process — it connects to Loom, registers, and serves node tasks.

item.title: Containers
item.description: Cortex is distributed as the metaloom/cortex-server image. It runs as a daemon: it connects to a Loom server, registers, and serves node tasks. See Container Images for the image overview.

item.title: Examples
item.description: The examples/ directory of the source repository contains three customer-facing examples showing how to extend Cortex with your own processing logic. They are deliberately lightweight: your code depends only on the slim Cortex node API (or, for Python, nothing but the wire protocol) and the Loom REST client — never on the Loom database, jOOQ or Postgres.

item.title: Features
item.description:
Media Processing

Cortex can process any media file type — images, videos, audio, and documents. The specific analyses performed depend on which nodes are active in a pipeline.

item.title: Maven Artifacts
item.description: All Cortex artifacts are published under the io.metaloom group and should generally be consumed with the shared BOM.

item.title: Monitoring API
item.description: A Cortex worker runs a lightweight monitoring HTTP server exposing liveness and readiness endpoints, designed for Kubernetes probes and load balancers. Loom exposes its own health check on the REST API.
